  EVIDENCE: OpenAI: The intake assembles the prompt, including issue/comment excerpts and failure logs, at lines 801–879. It freezes the scope inputs afterward, at lines 881–892. The added test only verifies that freezing precedes the diagnosis model launch, not that it precedes processing or assembling the untrusted evidence. Qwen: The last run diff adds `SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN` at lines 885-892, after the untrusted-evidence block (issue excerpts at 846-852, failure evidence at 854-857, run logs at 869-878) is redirected into `${PROMPT_FILE}` at line 879. The freeze happens before the diagnosis model runs (line 907), satisfying the second clause ("neither verbatim failure evidence nor a model-produced plan may widen it") because the scope inputs come from trusted sources only. But the literal ordering requirement — scope fixed before untrusted evidence is processed — is not met: the evidence is assembled into the prompt file six lines before the snapshot is written. The new test `test_intake_freezes_heal_scope_inputs_before_diagnosis` in `tests/test_heal_isolated_editor.py` asserts `freeze < diagnosis` (the codex call), which matches the implementation but does not assert `freeze < prompt_assembly`. The security property holds (scope inputs are trusted, model cannot widen), so this is a literal-ordering gap rather than a runtime defect.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_heal_isolated_editor.py:485-488 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The new test slices the function body by finding the literal `"\n}\n"` after the `_open_issue()\n` line. The function actually closes with `}` on its own line, and the surrounding shell has multiple `}`s (e.g. `|| exit 1` chains and the case statement). The test only fails if the literal sequence no longer appears, but it also cannot detect a regression where the snapshot read code is moved AFTER another `}` closer in the same function (e.g. an early `return 0`), so the slice would stop there and miss the post-snapshot read. More importantly, the test passes on the current code and does not exercise the `set -e` failure paths: the third `assert` (the `*.verified`/`DIAG_FILE` check) will pass even when those strings are absent because of the way the `split("compose-issue")[0]` slice is built, so the test provides weak coverage of the post-diagnosis read.
  WHY: not a runtime failure today; the test passes on the snapshot it asserts against. The concern is that the test is positioned to break loudly if the freeze is moved back, but it would also silently pass if the post-snapshot read is reintroduced anywhere before the first `}\n` of the case statement, because the `intake.index("\n}\n")` would still find a closing brace earlier in the file. The reviewer should flag this as a brittle contract test, not a runtime defect.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:885-892 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The scope freeze is now written from `LOG_DIR/*.verified` files that were created at line 280-308. Those files hold the raw, unauthenticated `.verified` JSON whose `referenced_paths` were extracted from the model's diagnosis-free run-info reads at line 286-295. The `referenced_paths` field comes from `run_json["referenced_workflows"]` which on a PR has not been authenticated against the consumer repository: the run-info read at line 286 uses `gh_api_json_to_file` which uses `GH_TOKEN`, but the run may belong to a foreign repository (e.g. a consumer triggering the dispatcher), so the `referenced_paths` list may include coding-workflows paths the consumer should not be able to influence. Today this is fine because the marker is then filtered by `_safe_heal_path` and `git ls-tree` at line 1088, and `git -C "${scope_checkout}" rev-parse --verify "${scope_ref}^{commit}"` requires the path to actually exist at the resolved commit. So the implicit trust expansion in `SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN` is bounded by the explicit `git ls-tree` check downstream. No runtime defect.
  WHY: does not fail at runtime today; the existing `git ls-tree` path verification at line 1088 prevents any foreign path from being written into the marker. Flagging as a trust-boundary note for awareness, not a defect.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:line 891-892
  PROBLEM: A `jq` parse failure inside any of the four `$(jq ... 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')` sub-shells would silently substitute the empty array and freeze a scope that omits legitimate workflow paths. Today the freeze write at line 891 does not check whether the `jq -n` invocation actually produced the five expected top-level keys.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: add a one-line assertion: `jq -e '.runs | type == "array" and .changed_files | type == "array"' "${SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f "${SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN}"; log "warn scope_inputs_freeze_failed"; }` after the write, so a malformed freeze is observable instead of silently emptied. Estimated lines changed: 3. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:line 894
  PROBLEM: When `SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN` is missing or empty, the freeze block at lines 885-892 will have logged `warn scope_inputs_freeze_failed` and removed the file, but the diagnosis still runs.
  WHY: Today `_open_issue` checks `[ -s "${SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN:-}" ]` (line 1088) and falls back to the unresolved branch correctly, so the only risk is operator observability. Suggested minimal fix: re-add `[ -s "${SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN:-}" ]` log line right before the diagnosis runs so the WARN shows up next to the model invocation as well, not just the freeze step. Estimated lines changed: 1. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
